findings.title: Impossible first small-coordinate requirement in the expander construction

items: Proof of Theorem B, delta_k=1/k and epsilon_k=100 sqrt(delta_k log(1/delta_k))

hypotheses_checked: Every n>=1 and d(n)>=n; V(n) is nonzero n-dimensional subspace
Orthogonal projection onto V has norm1; epsilon1=0
findings.decisive_evidence: The displayed strict requirement becomes1<0 for every such V. Exact symbolic projection and parameter calculations agree; first10 delta choices are also outside Lemma4 domain.
findings.core_dependency: Random subspace selection is the input to the TheoremB block embedding and CorollaryC.
findings.impact: Literal parameter choice impossible. Main embedding scope is preserved by an explicit repaired sequence and uniform block proof.
findings.repair_verification: Use delta_k=1/(k+10); epsilon_k=100 sqrt(delta_k log(1/delta_k)) tends0. For fixed n apply Lemma4 finitely many times and a union bound at sufficiently large dimension. Report supplies disjoint-block choice if necessary and controls finite initial blocks by their diameters.
findings.severity_basis: The required subspace does not exist for any n, so a core construction used by Theorem B and Corollary C fails as printed. A verified repair and the absence of a theorem counterexample limit the conclusion, but do not downgrade this core proof error.

findings.title: Undefined finite initial radii in Theorem A proof

items: Claim that Lemma1 applies for each n

hypotheses_checked: Nonempty uniformly locally finite metric space; concrete X=Z usual metric
For1<=n<=64, sqrt(n)/8<=1 and admissibility is strict
findings.decisive_evidence: The set defining the displayed radius is empty for1<=n<=64, so it cannot supply a positive admissible radius. Z has exact N_Z(R)=2floor(R)+1. This is an auxiliary formula defect, not a counterexample to the nonexistent embedding assumed for contradiction.
findings.core_dependency: TheoremA needs only an admissible radius tail tending to infinity.
findings.impact: Finite-prefix domain failure, without damage to the nonembedding conclusion after the explicit tail repair.
findings.repair_verification: Take J_n={j=1,...,n:64N_X(j)^2<n}. If empty choose a_n=0; otherwise r_n=max J_n and use Lemma1. For fixed integer j uniform local finiteness makes j in J_n eventually, proving eventual nonemptiness and r_n to infinity. Product/complementary-corner argument then works without normality assumptions.
findings.severity_basis: The failure is confined to finitely many initial indices outside the asymptotic radius tail actually needed. It does not invalidate that operative tail; this dependency distinction, rather than mere ease of repair, supports Minor.

scientific_checks.decision: confirmed; severity corrected Minor to Major
scientific_checks.independent_derivation: For every n>=1 the required n-dimensional subspace is nonzero, k=1 is among 1,...,n, delta1=1 and epsilon1=0. Taking E to be all d(n) coordinates gives projection norm1, so the required strict inequality is 1<0 for every possible choice. In addition the first ten delta values are outside Lemma4's strict domain.
scientific_checks.actual_dependency: The impossible selection is the block-subspace input for the quasi-local embedding of Theorem B and Corollary C. It invalidates a core construction at every stage, not only a dispensable initial block.
scientific_checks.counterevidence_and_repair: For delta_k=1/(k+10), every parameter lies in (0,1/10), epsilon_k tends0, and for each fixed n a finite union bound at sufficiently large expander dimension yields simultaneous requirements. The finite-prefix diameter control and disjoint-block construction in the report give uniform quasi-locality. This is positive evidence that the theorem can survive; it does not validate the printed impossible choice or downgrade a core proof error.
scientific_checks.scope: No counterexample to Theorems A/B/5 or Corollary C is established.

scientific_checks.independent_derivation: For every nonempty uniformly locally finite X and n<=64, N_X(R)>=1 makes N_X(R)<sqrt(n)/8 impossible. X=Z with its usual metric satisfies all metric hypotheses and N_X(R)=2floor(R)+1.
scientific_checks.actual_dependency_and_severity: Only a radius tail tending to infinity is used in the nonembedding contradiction; the finitely many failed initial indices are outside that operative tail. This supports Minor independently of repair length.
scientific_checks.repair: J_n={1<=j<=n:64N_X(j)^2<n}; for any fixed j uniform local finiteness makes it belong for all sufficiently large n. Set a_n=0 when J_n is empty; otherwise use max J_n. This preserves strict constants and avoids infinite suprema for finite spaces.
